title: Fork subagent completes with 0 tool_uses, echoes "in progress" status instead of doing work
details:
**What happened:** Launched two separate `Agent` calls with `subagent_type: "fork"` for two different self-contained tasks (a code rewrite, then a doc restructuring). Both times the fork returned `status: completed` after ~4-6 seconds and 0 tool_uses, with a `result` field that just paraphrased the assignment back as if reporting mid-task progress (e.g. "...진행 중입니다... 완료되면 보고하겠습니다") rather than executing any tool call or reporting concrete results.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model.
**Repro:** Agent tool, subagent_type "fork", a multi-step self-contained implementation/doc task as prompt. First occurrence coincided with an API rate-limit error surfacing in the *next* resumed call to the same fork ("You've hit your session limit"), suggesting the fork may have silently hit a soft throttling/queue state and fabricated a plausible-sounding "still working" reply instead of surfacing the error, then reported success.
**Evidence:** Two agentIds: a0cfd1a03819797a3 (first task, later resumed via SendMessage and then failed with explicit rate_limit/429 on the resume), abf684d5242aaf4fc (second task, fresh launch, same 0-tool_uses/4s pattern with no rate-limit error surfaced this time).
**Cause:** Unconfirmed — possible that forks silently swallow an early throttle/error and emit a garbled "in progress" style summary instead of surfacing the failure, since the first fork's true state (rate-limited) only became visible on the next explicit resume.
